front.title: Workload Identity Tokens in Automated Certificate Management Environment (ACME) Orders

abstract.t:
Enterprises hold large certificate inventories, yet few of their certificates are managed through ACME. Many workloads, such as CI/CD jobs, containers, virtual machines, cloud services and the automation that manages appliances, cannot complete ACME's challenges. Certification Authorities (CAs) and Certificate Lifecycle Management (CLM) systems that serve them fall back to External Account Binding (EAB) with long-lived shared secrets, or to proprietary APIs.
OpenID Connect (OIDC) provides a short-lived cryptographically verified identity token to the workload. This document lets an ACME client send that token with each newOrder request. The token can be bound to the request's nonce and account key through its audience claim, so identity providers need no changes. The CA/CLM verifies the token and, under its own policy, may pre-authorize the identifier in the order, as RFC 8555 already allows. This replaces the EAB secret with a fresh, per-order proof of workload identity. It does not change how CAs validate control of identifiers.
